name: Protectorate General to Pacify the South
wikipedia: Protectorate General to Pacify the South

predecessors.name: Tang dynasty
predecessors.text: 'In 679, the Annan Protectorate replaced the Jiaozhou Protectorate' (also called Jiaozhi), 'located in modern-day Vietnam'; Jiaozhou had covered parts of modern Guangdong, Guangxi and northern Vietnam

successors.name: Jinghai Circuit
successors.text: 'Gao Pian ... recaptured Songping, the capital of Annan' and 'renamed the region of Annan to Jinghai Jun' after 866

ledger.x: 679: the Annan Protectorate replaces the Jiaozhou Protectorate.

wars.name: Liu Yanyou's tax revolt (Lý Tự Tiên and Đinh Kiến)
wars.outcome: Liu Yanyou's attempt to levy full taxes on the Li people sparked a revolt that took Songping; Cao Xuanjing put it down.

wars.name: Revolt of Mai Thúc Loan
wars.outcome: Mai Thúc Loan rebelled in what is now Hà Tĩnh in 722 and was defeated in 723.

wars.name: Revolt of Phùng Hưng
wars.outcome: Do Anh Han, Phung Hung and Phung An rebelled against doubled taxes in 785 and the Tang retook Annan in 791.

wars.name: Huanwang (Champa) seizure of southern Annan
wars.outcome: A northern Cham state, Huanwang, seized southern Annan in 803 and 'the Chinese barely defeated the Cham and recovered lost regions in 809'.

wars.name: Tang-Nanzhao conflicts in Annan
wars.outcome: Nanzhao raided from 846 and 858, briefly took Songping on 17 January 861 (retaken 21 July), took it again on 28 February 863 and held it until Gao Pian retook Annan in autumn 866.

certainty.note: No frontier is drawn on either page; the southern and western limits are the researcher's reading.
